item.title: County to revisit Forest Service reimbursement cap
item.description: Box Elder County commissioners renewed a cooperative law enforcement patrol contract with the U.S. Forest Service on Wednesday while acknowledging that the current $6,000 reimbursement cap no longer reflects actual patrol costs. The contract allows the sheriff’s office to patrol National Forest System lands within the county, including areas of the Cache National Forest and the Sawtooth National Forest. item.title: County approves cemetery board appointments
item.description: The Box Elder County Commission approved three cem­etery board appointments and ratified a previously signed beer license consent form during its Feb. 11 meeting. item.title: Perry 2025 audit shows city in strong financial position with clean opinion
item.description: An audit of Perry City’s financial statements shows the city remains in a strong fi­nancial position and contin­ues to follow proper account­ing and regulatory practices. David Rogers of Davis & Bott CPAs presented the city’s fiscal year 2025 financial statements to the Perry City Council on Thursday, high­lighting growth in the city’s overall net position and solid fund balances. item.title: State of the City highlights ‘a lot of good things’ that happened in Perry

item.description: The Box Elder County Sheriff’s Office is clari­fying how recently donated surplus radios from Brigham City will be used and how they relate to previously approved county radio upgrades. item.title: UTA threatens Perry with legal action over city’s 2023 repeal of transportation tax
item.description: Responding to threats of legal action from the Utah Transit Authority, the Perry City Council last week reinstated a .30% sales tax that helps fund the UTA. The council voted unanimously Jan. 22 to ap­prove Ordinance 26-A, severing what it described as “invalid portions” of a 2023 ordinance that repealed the UTA tax in December 2023.
